status: PROPOSED, UNREGISTERED. Not a pre-specified rule until its sha256 is registered in research/preregistrations.jsonl before forward data (after 2026-09-24) is used to evaluate it. The director decides whether to register it.
rule_type: Wald SPRT (Sequential Probability Ratio Test), one look per calendar month, on the monthly window excess return net of the frozen base cost.

statistic.definition: x_n = (window n's TLT return over its 3 held sessions, minus the T-bill return accrued over the same sessions) minus 4 bp (base cost, 2 bp/side x 2 sides: entry + exit). Equivalently: win_ex - 0.0004, where win_ex reproduces reports/audit_tsy/e_postpub.json's window_ex figures exactly.
statistic.look_cadence: one look at the close of each month's last held session (the same close that ends book M's position), i.e. one look per month, matching the ~12 windows/year of the frozen spec.

hypotheses.H0_kill: true mean = -0.000400 (gross edge exactly zero; base cost still paid)
hypotheses.H1_confirm: true mean = 0.001564 (the post-publication, 2019-10..2026-08 sample mean, net of base cost -- world W2 in reports/future_lab2/results.json)

sigma_source: sample std (ddof=1) of win_ex over the full 2003-01..2026-08 history (284 months; reports/audit_tsy/c_months_{dev,val}.csv), fixed and not re-estimated on forward data.
decision_rule: CONFIRM (accept H1) at the first month where LLR_n >= A = 2.7726.
KILL (accept H0) at the first month where LLR_n <= B = -1.5581.

At 120 months (10 years) with no decision: END_NO_DECISION -- stays forward observation only; this cap is a reporting convention of this lab, not part of the SPRT itself, which in principle continues until it exits (mu1-mu0)/sigma^2)-scaled boundaries.
evaluator: research.future_lab2.rule.sprt_run(X, mu0, mu1, sigma, alpha=0.05, beta=0.2), X = the realised monthly x_n sequence from forward_start onward
forward_start: 2026-09-24 (per reports/tsy_month_end/ADDENDUM_AUDIT_2026-09-23.md: forward judgement uses only data after this date, with official closes)

operating_characteristics.note: The SPRT is sequential and on average decides faster than the fixed-sample test above at the same alpha/beta, but the fixed-sample number is the right answer to 'how long for 80% power' since the SPRT's own decision time is itself a random variable (see sprt_oc.csv / results.json for its simulated distribution per world).
operating_characteristics.full_operating_characteristics: reports/future_lab2/tsy_sprt.csv and results.json (tsy.sprt), simulated under W0-W5, 8000+ paths, seed 20260924

not_evidence: mu1 and sigma are estimated from already-observed history, including the same window effect this rule will judge. The rule tests whether forward data is consistent with that history; it cannot anticipate a regime absent from it. It also does not use a haircut/sceptical-prior structure the way research/future_lab/forward.py's Bayesian rule does -- it is deliberately the simplest classical rule that matches the brief's alpha/beta request.
limitations: sigma is treated as known and fixed; in truth it is estimated once from 284 months of history and could itself be wrong (e.g. under W4's vol x1.5, the true sigma is 50% higher than what this rule assumes, which changes its effective alpha/beta -- see W4's row in tsy_sprt.csv, where the rule's actual error rates drift from the nominal 5%/20%).

H1 is pinned to the post-publication mean; a candidate that is real but weaker (e.g. W3's decaying edge) will often drift into KILL well before it would under W2, because the rule has no notion of a time-varying mean.
The rule only ever chooses between exactly two points (mu0, mu1); it is not a test of 'is there some edge', only of 'does the data look like mu0 or like mu1'.
